This writ petition has been filed challenging the award dated 2.1.2023 passed by respondent no.2
i.e. Special Land Acquisition Officer/ Competent Authority, District Moradabad.
2.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the award dated 2.1.2023 was passed in ignorance of provisions of Section 3G(7) of the National Highways Act, 1956 and also that the award ignored the provisions of Section 26 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

3. Learned counsel for the petitioners has relied upon the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Godrej Sara Lee Ltd. Vs. The Excise and Taxation Officer-cum-Assessing Authority and others, AIR 2023 (SC) 781 and has specifically relied upon the paragraph no. 37 of it, which is reproduced herein as under:-
"37.

entities.text: Godrej Sara Lee Ltd. Vs. The Excise and Taxation Officer-cum-Assessing Authority and others, AIR 2023 (SC) 781
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: A decision may be questioned as suffering from an illegality if its maker fails to understand the law that regulates his decision making power correctly or if he fails to give effect to any law that holds the field and binds the parties.

On the other hand,
having regard to the purpose section 34 seeks to serve, to take exception to a decision on the ground of lack of propriety of any proceedings or order passed in such proceedings, it essentially ought to relate to a procedural impropriety.
It is incumbent for the accuser to show that the decision maker has failed to observe the standard procedures applicable in case of exercise of his power.

Additionally, to impeach an order on the ground of moral impropriety, it has to be shown that the weight of facts together with the applicable law overwhelmingly points to one course of action but the decision has surprisingly gone the other way, giving reason to suspect misbehaviour or misconduct in the sphere of activity of the decision maker warranting a revision."
4. Learned counsel for the petitioners has also relied upon the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Whirpool Corporation Vs. Registrar of Trade Marks, Mumbai and others, AIR 1999 (SC)
22 and has submitted that the alternative remedy is not an absolute bar.

entities.text: Whirpool Corporation Vs. Registrar of Trade Marks, Mumbai and others, AIR 1999 (SC)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 5. Having heard the learned counsel for the petitioners, learned Standing Counsel and Sri Gambhir Tripathi, learned counsel for respondent no.3-National Highway Authority of India, we are of the view that the law as has been laid down in the case of Godrej Sara Lee Ltd. Vs. The Excise and Taxation Officer-cum-Assessing Authority and others, AIR 2023 (SC) 781 definitely is the law and in accordance with which, the case has to be decided.

entities.text: Godrej Sara Lee Ltd. Vs. The Excise and Taxation Officer-cum-Assessing Authority and others, AIR 2023 (SC) 781
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioners, if they approach the arbitrator under Section 3G(7) of the National Highways Act, 1956, the Court expects that the case would be decided in accordance with law.

Undoubtedly, the Supreme Court has stated that approaching the High Court under Article 226 of the Constitution of India is not an absolute bar where an alternative remedy is provided, but we consider that the petitioners have an appropriate alternative remedy for approaching the arbitrator and no specific ground has been made out by the petitioners to knock the doors of the High Court directly.

6. Under such circumstances, without going into further controversy, we direct that if the petitioners file an application before the arbitrator as is provided under Section 3G(5) of the National Highways Act, 1956 within a period of ten days from today then the same shall be decided within a period of six months from the date of production of certified copy of this order.
6. With these observations, the writ petition is disposed of.
